report:
Reviewed the complete claim: (1) the checked signature is a cross-item semantic interface; (2) its types, generic binder, and parameter environment are available without checking its definition's body; (3) signature computation does not read function bodies. The referenced architectural-foundations section explicitly distinguishes semantic body dependencies from provisional coarse CST invalidation/backdating, so obtaining a CST containing a body pointer is not itself semantic body checking.

All eight ordinary implementation entries were inspected. local_syms/fns.rs::sig reads declaration generics, parameters, receivers, result, and predicates, never cst.body. It constructs FnSig and Binder in its own target stash. Its open_owner reads only trait/impl signatures; local_syms/traits.rs::sig builds Self and declaration predicates, and local_syms/impls.rs::sig builds the self type, trait header and predicates without opening associated bodies. cst/generics.rs mints generic identities from declaration data and binds them in the resolver. cst/ty.rs recursively checks only type syntax, represents named aliases without checking their bodies, and obtains external ADT declaration facts. check/trait_env.rs lowers declared bounds/where clauses and consults trait signatures, not methods. check/sig.rs::complete_parameter_env merges declaration and type-use predicates; finish publishes the independently owned result. external_syms.rs::external_fn_signature requests keyed fn_signature metadata and lower_fn_signature builds parameter/result types, owner/method generics and predicate environment from those owned facts. The external trait, impl and ADT paths likewise lower declaration metadata. This source inspection finds no body-checking path in these signature producers. Missing receivers, unsupported generic/predicate forms and unavailable external facts produce eligibility flags or unavailable metadata, not body fallback. Conversely LocalFnSym::body imports the previously computed signature and only then dereferences cst.body, demonstrating the dependency direction.

The complete associated test set is the single explicit TODO sage_meta::todo::checking_signature_body_independence. It contains no assertions and establishes no executed semantic coverage. Its documented outstanding matrix is appropriate: source fixtures for local and external callers must assert the selected interface facts and absence of body queries, then perform a body-only edit and assert signature equality and no consumer reexecution. Completing that fixture/query-trace and edit observation matrix is the prerequisite for ordinary test evidence; this review preserves the honest TODO and does not describe the placeholder as a passing verification. In particular an accidental future body() demand would not be detected by this placeholder. No ordinary test or N/A entry is being omitted.

Added essential implementation associations at the seven helper/owner/external locations before restarting the review; initial fragments now cover all of them. Additional architecture/policy/module context is captured via review read. Ran cargo fmt and cargo build successfully (build emitted warnings); no behavioral test was run and no runtime absence-of-body trace is claimed. Central delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity checks are owned by the coordinator. No behavior or expectations were modified. The source review is accepted with the existing explicit test deferral, not as a proof or completed runtime verification.
